picks.what: Bird’s-eye view in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 5
picks.why: colored true view of the upper town on its cliffs above the Alzette

picks.what: Engraving in Merian’s Topographia Circuli Burgundici (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: labeled prospect of the town with church towers and walls

picks.what: The fortress from the Obergrünewald, pen-and-ink drawing (Albertina, Vienna)
picks.why: detailed view over the fortress walls into the town

picks.what: The upper town above the Passerelle viaduct, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color general view, cathedral spires and the viaduct

picks.what: The Grund and the fortifications at dusk, photograph
picks.why: the classic view of the lower town, Neumünster Abbey and the casemate cliffs

gaps: P0: none (Nuremberg Chronicle items are portraits and family trees); P5: none (the 1945 and 1964 aerials show Mertert, Grevenmacher and Wasserbillig, not the city)
notes: #6’s file name says Blaeu 1649, but it is the Braun and Hogenberg vol. 5 view (the same plate appears in #8, a 1617 edition of vol. 5, with the gutter through it). #6 is only 1024 px wide; if that is too soft, #5 (vol. 3 bird’s-eye plan, first published 1581, 3405 px, colored) is the fallback, with y 1581. #11–#13, #19–#21 and #31 show the Palais and Jardin du Luxembourg in Paris. #15 is the right-hand third of Callot’s long panorama; #17 (the whole panorama) is only 1600×310.
